images.filename: Northbound platform at Rannoch railway staiton.jpg
images.caption:
The northbound platform at Rannoch railway station in Perth and Kinross, central Scotland. From this platform you can catch a train to Fort William, trains to Glasgow depart from the other side of the building. An exhibition on railways in the Scottish Highlands was due to open in the station building about a fortnight after my visit - although the leaflet we picked up about it didn't say this!
Truly in the middle of almost nowhere, Rannoch station is at the end of a five-mile dead-end road and 16 miles distant from the large (for the area) village of Kinloch Rannoch at the far end of Loch Rannoch (Map).

images.filename: Departing Rannoch Station - geograph.org.uk - 730642.jpg
images.caption: Departing Rannoch Station The overnight sleeper service from London departs Rannoch with 35 lonely miles left to its final destination at Fort William. An attempt to discontinue this service in the 1990s was met with a storm of protest and questions were asked in Parliament. The media dubbed it the 'Deerstalker Express', characterising the typical passenger as a London businessman heading to the Highlands for a shooting weekend; whatever the reality, it is certainly a romantic and spectacular journey.

images.filename: A Scottish Adventure- The Jacobite over Glenfinnan Viaduct.jpg
images.caption:
Day 4 of the Scottish Adventure sees me stood on a muddy, wet hill side near Glenfinnan Viaduct, awaiting for the Jacobite to come round the curve and into view. The pleasing sight of the train coming into view was one of the most impressive I have seen for years, an incredible sight to say the least. Providing power is LNER Thompson/peppercorn Class K1 62005 "Lord of the Isles". The train is running from Fort William - Mallaig along the West Highland Line, considered the most sceninc railway line in the UK.
The viaduct is known for many as being used in the Harry Potter movies, which the Jacobite stock was also used in. Hills and mountains around the viaduct only add to the atmosphere of the area.

The headcode is 2Y61 10:15 Fort William - Mallaig
